notes: The exact R01 packet and all final task packets are authentic, every prior task finding remains closed, and independent replay passed all 38 selected TypeScript/renderer cases and all 54 selected Python contract/schema/repository/service cases. Slice approval is nevertheless unavailable because one high-severity cross-task integration defect remains at the large-lineage boundary. The repository materializes the entire bounded graph, silently stops traversal at 20,000 revisions, and converts a real has-more condition to nextCursor=null when the next offset would exceed 10,000. The generated client accepts that terminal response, and the renderer labels and exports the accumulated prefix as complete. This contradicts the approved plan's streaming requirement and the task/slice promise that complete verified export contains every fact inside the accepted depth/direction bounds. The R01 evidence also contains no representative lineage benchmark with the required hardware, repetitions/distribution, and regression threshold; that missing evidence is consolidated into the same unmodeled-large-graph finding rather than opened separately.

checks.check: large-lineage completeness, continuation, and resource boundary
checks.details: At exact state a488842, repositories.py lines 2037-2082 stops breadth-first traversal when the visited/frontier budget reaches 20,000 without adding missing/integrity/truncation state. Lines 2165-2169 first materialize all lineage nodes and then compute has_more, but line 2167 returns null whenever the true next offset exceeds 10,000. Deterministic reproduction with cursor=10,000, pageSize=100, and nodeCount=10,101 yields pageLength=100, hasMore=true, hiddenFacts=1, and returnedNextCursor=null. AuditLineageWorkspace.tsx lines 182-221 treats null as terminal and emits completeness=complete. The approved plan explicitly requires large graphs to stream rather than materialize completely and requires a representative benchmark; neither the implementation nor the R01 evidence satisfies that boundary.

findings.title: Large lineage limits silently produce an incomplete manifest labeled complete
findings.acceptanceBoundary: CAP-03.S03 slice outcome; T03 criterion 1; approved slice plan Sections 6, 10, 11, 15, and 17
findings.reproduction: At exact integrated state a488842b6b37e3a1b68873f257e75285b03442e3, arrange a verified lineage containing at least 10,101 returned facts inside the accepted revision, direction, and maxDepth bounds, then request pageSize=100 through cursor=10,000. In services/core-api/src/research_observatory_core/repositories.py, page=nodes[10000:10100] contains 100 facts and has_more is true because 10,100 < 10,101, but next_cursor becomes null because 10,100 is greater than the hard 10,000 cursor ceiling. The response remains integrityState=verified and exportAllowed=true. The generated client validates only non-null cursor progress, so it accepts the response. mergeLineagePage preserves nextCursor=null, lineageManifestReady returns true after the accumulated pages, and exportLineageManifest writes completeness=complete although at least one fact was never returned. Independently, a breadth/depth-bounded graph whose frontier remains nonempty after 20,000 visited revisions is silently truncated by the absolute_scan_limit loop and can follow the same verified/exportable path. The query also reconstructs and materializes all nodes for every page instead of streaming. A PowerShell replay of the exact pagination predicate produced cursor=10000, pageLength=100, nodeCount=10101, hasMore=True, returnedNextCursor=null, hiddenFacts=1, and rendererTreatsTerminal=True.
findings.impact: A researcher can export a content-minimized manifest that asserts complete, verified provenance while omitting accepted-bound lineage facts. That is a false evidence-completeness claim at the central scholarly traceability boundary. The same design performs project-wide integrity reconstruction and full graph materialization on every page, with no plan-required benchmark establishing acceptable latency or memory behavior.
findings.requiredRemediation: In a strict-descendant slice remediation, define one explicit large-lineage contract across Core, OpenAPI/generated client, and renderer. Never return a terminal cursor or permit complete export while accepted-bound facts or an unvisited frontier remain. Use a continuation/snapshot design that can advance beyond the current offset ceiling or return an explicit truncated/incomplete integrity disposition that is read-only and non-exportable. Replace full per-page graph/node materialization with bounded streaming or an equivalent indexed snapshot consistent with the approved architecture. Add real SQLite/Core/generated-client/renderer regressions at both limits, including more than 10,100 facts and a frontier-over-scan-budget case, and prove restart/stable ordering, rights/integrity monotonicity, and export denial or true completion. Record the Section 11 representative hardware/OS, fixture version, warm/cold state, repetitions/distribution, absolute budget, and regression threshold. Preserve every prior task closure and the protected witness.

closures.details: Independent contract replay confirms lifecycle/status/relation-role truth, exact revision and identity closure, cross-kind restrictions, PortableKey/UTC parity, and safe future event behavior remain closed in generated TypeScript and Python.

Independent repository/service replay confirms exact migration suffixes, atomic output/provenance/outbox/checkpoint authority, v1/v2 chain compatibility, replay binding, corruption denial, retry/restart, and actor/trace/outbox integrity closures remain valid. The new finding concerns unmodeled query cardinality, not a reopening of these transaction-integrity findings.

Independent replay confirms real typed lineage, approved workspace regions, strict ordinary cursor progress/termination, immutable query authority, monotonic rights/integrity denial, and missing/legacy fail-closed export remain fixed for the tested bounded fixtures. The new finding is distinct: Core itself falsely emits terminal null when hidden accepted-bound facts remain beyond a hard cardinality limit, so the client cannot infer the omission from the response.
